response:
Diagnosis: gen 5 confirmed and sharpened the mechanism. Both peak-intensity denominators work, but differently: capx/ppent maximizes alpha (-5.4%, t=-5.22) while capx/sale maximizes the cross-sectional slope (FMB -5.61, alpha -4.1%, t=-4.72) — they are measuring over-replacement of installed capital versus capacity ahead of demand, so they are complementary rather than redundant. Adding goodwill lifted alpha to -6.6% and Sharpe to -0.545 but cut coverage to 0.070 and halved the FMB slope, confirming the goodwill state is a non-linear tail effect that needs a monotone conditioner to be linearized (productivity did that partly: FMB -2.40; margin alone did not: -0.68). Two conditioner comparisons are now settled: industry-adjusted revenue per employee dominates gross margin, and both dominate R&D intensity (Peak_Capex_Knowledge_Starved: FMB -1.62 at 0.061 coverage), while recognized intangible formation flows added nothing (FMB -1.23). On the long side, importing productivity and the five-year investment state finally produced a coherent positive slope (FMB 2.43, alpha +3.0%, t=3.08). This batch consolidates the two denominators, tests conditioner smoothing, repairs the goodwill family's slope with a dual moat, rebuilds the long side, and opens two genuinely new state variables (plant age; investment-policy instability).

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Dual_Denominator_Peak_Capex_Unproductive
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, sale), 5)), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(sale, emp))))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm is unambiguously overexpanding when capital spending is simultaneously at a five-year peak relative to its installed plant and relative to its revenue base; conditioned on low organizational productivity, this doubly-confirmed capacity buildup should be the strongest short state in the cross-section.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The two normalizations produced the archive's best alpha and best FMB slope respectively, and they can disagree — a firm replacing old plant without adding capacity scores high on one and low on the other — so requiring both should purify the overinvestment state and improve both metrics at once. Coverage stays near maximum since only capx, ppent, sale, and emp are needed.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Peak_Capex_Persistent_Low_Productivity
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, sale), 5), NEG(IND_ADJ(MA(RATIO(sale, emp), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: Organizational capital is a slow-moving stock, so a three-year average of industry-adjusted revenue per employee measures it better than a single noisy year, and grading peak capital spending by this persistent measure should improve both the slope and the stability of the short leg.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This isolates one design choice — smoothing the intangible conditioner — against the best-FMB signal in the archive, holding the investment leg fixed. If alpha and Sharpe improve, the mispricing is about structural organizational weakness rather than a transitory productivity dip, which would guide the final consolidation; if it degrades, the conditioner is picking up recent operating news and should stay unsmoothed.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Fresh_Plant_Unproductive_Operator
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ppent, ppegt), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(sale, emp))))
HYPOTHESIS: The undepreciated share of gross plant measures how recently a firm's physical capacity was built; a young, largely unamortized asset base in the hands of a firm with weak organizational productivity represents freshly sunk capital that will not earn its cost.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This is a new state variable — capital vintage from the ppent-to-ppegt ratio — that summarizes years of cumulative physical expansion in a single persistent stock measure, rather than the flow-based peaks tested so far, so it should generate low-turnover portfolios and test whether the anomaly is about the spending act or the resulting capital overhang. It requires only widely reported items, so coverage should match the front-runners.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Goodwill_Overhang_Dual_Moat
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(gdwl, sale), SUMRANK(NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(sale, emp))), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Acquired goodwill is most likely to be impaired when the acquirer can neither operate efficiently nor price with power, so grading goodwill intensity by both intangible-advantage deficits should identify failed integrations with a monotone gradient rather than only in the tail.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The goodwill family carries the archive's largest alphas (-6.6% to -6.7%, |t|>4) but its FMB slope has never exceeded -2.4, and productivity conditioning was the only thing that moved it; adding the second, partly independent moat proxy is the natural next step to linearize the relation without diluting the alpha. Coverage will remain near 0.078 because goodwill reporting is the binding constraint, which is an accepted cost for this specific channel.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Funded_Productive_Innovator_Capex_Discipline
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(sale, emp)), SUMRANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(xrd, sale), RATIO(che, at)), NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: The long-side counterpart of the anomaly is a productive, research-intensive, cash-funded firm that is holding physical capital spending below its own historical norm; its economic capital is expensed and its restraint is misread as lack of growth.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Two independent long-side channels each delivered roughly 3% alpha with t near 3.1 — liquidity-plus-research and productivity-plus-research-plus-restraint — and only the latter produced a positive FMB slope (2.43), so combining the liquidity leg with the productivity-graded version should raise alpha reliability while preserving the gradient. This is the only long-side proposal in the batch, which matters because a tradable spread needs a defensible long leg, not just a short leg.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Erratic_Capital_Budget_Weak_Organization
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(VOL(RATIO(capx, sale), 5), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(sale, emp))))
HYPOTHESIS: Volatile capital spending relative to revenue indicates an undisciplined, stop-start investment policy; in firms that also lack organizational productivity it signals weak governance and poor project selection, predicting low returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This opens a second-moment channel never tested in the archive — the instability rather than the level or peak of investment intensity — and it is economically distinct because a firm can have volatile investment without ever reaching a five-year peak. Pairing it with the proven productivity conditioner keeps the intangible interaction intact at full coverage, and a null result would usefully confirm that only the level/state of overexpansion is priced.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
